title: The death of Ealasaid Chiar
summary: Ealasaid Chiar dies at sixty, having reigned thirty-one years and had the first king-list written, and is carried up the mountain road to lie among Sliochd Ìomhair. Her son takes the hall after her.

title: The roll falls silent
summary: After Ealasaid Chiar's son and granddaughter, Clàr nan Rìghrean Tormod began keeps no ruler's name for a span the reciters cannot close. Clàr an Talla at Dùn ìseal keeps its own count through the same years, naming Coimheadaichean na Lasrach where the hall names none.

title: Talla na Lasrach's clerks learn the stag-letters
summary: Shamed that it cannot read its own roll without borrowing another order's letters, Talla na Lasrach sets two of its own clerks to learn the stag-letters, taught by a stag-teacher paid in coal for the winter. From that year Talla na Lasrach keeps its roll in its own hand.

title: A Keeper named in the silent years
summary: A Keeper is named at Dùn ìseal of whom the roll keeps only the years of her reign, twenty-two, and the year of her death; of the rest of it nothing is told, the households burning their handful and the carriers walking their roads as their grandparents had.

title: The birth of Conall Dubh
summary: A household above Cnoc bheag, keeping sheep in sight of the wood the island has never cleared, has its fourth child, a son they name Conall and call Dubh for the black hair he is born with.

title: Conall Dubh sees the black horned beast
summary: At twenty years old, going up before first light to bring down strayed ewes, Conall Dubh meets a black horned beast at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, standing and watching him before it turns back into the trees. His mother believes him.

title: The watch grows to nine
summary: Conall Dubh's sister and two cousins join his watch at the wood's edge, and within five years of his own first sighting nine keep it by turns, waiting on a beast none of them can explain to a stranger's satisfaction.

title: The wood called sacred
summary: The watchers, near thirty now and housed in a turf hut at the wood's edge, are named the wood-watchers by the people of Cathair dhearg, and a clerk of Talla na Lasrach counting the season's coal is the first outsider to write Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag sacred in his own report.

title: The death of a teaching elder
summary: In the second winter of the two orders' silence over the cut tree, the teacher who first spoke for Scoiltean nan Draoidhean dies of an ordinary winter cough. Conall Dubh crosses to the teaching-circle unbidden to say he is sorry for their loss, the first word either side has spoken to the other.

title: Fearchar Òg brought to the hall
summary: A boy of seven, a great-grandson of the house that once held Dùn dhearg, is brought to Dùn ìseal by his mother's hand and acknowledged heir by Coimheadaiche na Lasrach of that year, the first claim in longer than the roll can say with certainty found worth Talla na Lasrach's confidence.

title: Calum Liath takes the flame
summary: Calum Liath is made Keeper at forty-five, in Fearchar Òg's ninth year, and judges at once that the wood-watchers and Scoiltean nan Draoidhean will share their silence forever unless someone outside both orders sets a boundary between them.

title: Conall Dubh walks the eastern wood
summary: The day after the last boundary stone is set, Conall Dubh walks unarmed into Coille Naomh Muileann chiar for the first time in his life, a guest under the terms he helped make, and stands a while at the border stand before turning home.
